messages:
Maya (AE): Heads-up — prospect (MedixOne) wants to run a 60-day EU pilot but procurement insists on a bank guarantee + they require NET60 after pilot. They're pushing for our entity on the beneficiary and want wet-ink on the guarantee. Can legal/finance advise on routing and whether we can accept NET60 for conversion to production? @Alex (legal) @Nora (finance)

Alex (legal): Two main options: 1) Direct orderform + MSA where we can accept an irrevocable standby LC naming Redwood Inference, Inc. 2) Marketplace subscription (no LC possible). Wet-ink on the LC is common from European banks but we can accept bank's scanned originals plus SWIFT/MT760 confirmation. For NET60 post-pilot we need credit approval; won't sign conversion with NET60 unless customer credit check passes or they provide a payment guarantee.

Ravi (solutions): Technical constraints: to meet EU-only processing and SOC2-ish compliance for the pilot, we'll need a dedicated tenant in eu-central-1 and customer-managed KMS if they insist. That adds ~EUR 2.4k/month and 2-4 business days provisioning. Also if they convert to marketplace later, some features (private KMS) won't carry over cleanly.

Nora (finance): Finance can accept an LC for the pilot if it's irrevocable and references the orderform number. For conversion terms: NET60 is OK for enterprise deals but requires AE to log credit request & revenue ops approval. We prefer conversion to prepaid or charged via marketplace for SaaS. If they insist on NET60, add a security deposit or extend LC to cover first invoice post-conversion.

Maya (AE): Customer PO snippet:
```
PO#: MX-2026-4521
Term: 60-day pilot
Amount: EUR 11,000
Payment: Bank guarantee / irrevocable standby LC (Bank: EuroBank AG)
Billing: ap@medixone.eu
Conversion intent: Move to production on completion, prefer NET60
```

Alex (legal): I'll draft an orderform redline with: LC must reference orderform number and Redwood Inference, Inc.; LC expiry >= 30 days after pilot end; acceptance tests for pilot; clause: pilot automatically terminates unless parties sign conversion order; data processing limited to EU; SCCs/EU Addendum executed. If they want NET60 on conversion, we should require either a new LC or a deposit to cover first NET60 invoice.

SignBot: DocSignature: Envelope prepared for MedixOne. Countersign flow requires customer signer + bank contact for LC docs.

Maya (AE): Plan: I'll ask customer whether digital SWIFT confirmation + scanned LC originals is acceptable to avoid wet-ink delays. I'll also surface the additional EU pilot cost and ask if they can cover it or offset during conversion. Next: Alex to post redline (ETA 6h), Nora to confirm exact LC wording treasury needs (ETA 3h), Ravi to confirm provisioning ETA.

Nora (finance): Quick note: treasury will not accept LC that names AWS as beneficiary. If customer pushes marketplace, explain that payment terms cannot be guaranteed by LC under AWS marketplace model.

Maya (AE): Thanks — will loop back after procurement call in 90 mins. :phone:
